title: Whitened correlated sign summands
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $-1<\\rho<1$. Let $a_1,\\ldots,a_n\\in\\mathbb R$ satisfy $\\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\\le\\varepsilon$ for every $i$. Choose a pair $(x,y)$ of sign vectors in $\\{\\pm1\\}^n$ by taking $x$ uniformly at random and, independently in each coordinate, setting $y_i=x_i$ with probability $(1+\\rho)/2$ and $y_i=-x_i$ otherwise. For each $i$, form $v_i=a_i(x_i,y_i)\\in\\mathbb R^2$ and apply the inverse positive square root of the matrix $\\begin{pmatrix}1&\\rho\\\\\\rho&1\\end{pmatrix}$. The sum over $i$ of the expected cubed Euclidean norms of these transformed vectors is at most $4\\varepsilon/\\sqrt{1-\\rho^2}$.�
